title: Ada and the Landfall
premise: Riverboat captain Kestrel Marchetti agrees to ferry a dying prospector's map upriver before monsoon season seals the delta, only to discover the cargo includes the prospector's estranged daughter, Ada, who believes her father abandoned her years ago. As rival salvagers and a corrupt magistrate close in, Kestrel must choose between honoring her promise to keep the map's secret — a drowned settlement holding proof of the magistrate's stolen land grants — and protecting the crew she's grown to love. When the monsoon makes landfall early, Kestrel and Ada race the flood to deliver the evidence to a river tribunal of boatfolk who govern by their own law. The expedition returns home battered but whole: justice is served outside any courtroom, Ada claims her inheritance on her own terms, and Kestrel finally lets go of the debt that has anchored her.
about_author: Paloma Sterling is the pen name of a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on tropical rivers before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. Her fiction draws on the boatfolk's oral traditions, blending salt-crusted adventure with quiet meditations on memory and obligation.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At a muddy river landing, a fever-wracked prospector named Elias Vane offers Kestrel his life's savings and a sealed map in exchange for one promise: carry it to the headwaters before the rains, tell no one what it shows. Kestrel, drowning in debt on her boat the Magpie, accepts. Emotional beat: wary hope — a bargain that feels too easy.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Ada
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At the next port, a young woman forces her way aboard claiming passage north: Ada Vane, who hasn't seen her father in nine years and doesn't know he's dying. Kestrel hides both the map and Elias's condition, torn between duty and decency. Emotional beat: guilt tightening like a mooring line as Ada talks about the father who 'abandoned' her.

chapters.title: Sandbar Justice
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Salvagers led by the magistrate's enforcer, Corben Hale, board the Magpie demanding inspection. The crew deflects them with a staged argument and a forged manifest, but Ada glimpses the map's edge and realizes Kestrel is lying about something. Emotional beat: first flicker of trust between the women, shadowed by Ada's suspicion.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A night run through fog; Kestrel finally tells Ada her father is alive but failing, upstream, waiting. Ada's fury cracks into grief, and she demands to see the map. Kestrel refuses — a promise is a promise. Emotional beat: love against duty, both women bleeding a little.

chapters.title: The Drowned Town
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. They detour around a storm and pass the flooded ruins of Merrow's Landing, where Ada deciphers enough of the overheard coordinates to understand: the map marks land the magistrate seized illegally after the flood that killed the town. Emotional beat: revelation — the debt Elias carried was never money; it was testimony.

chapters.title: Hale's Bargain
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hale corners the Magpie at a lock and offers Kestrel a clean slate — her debt erased — if she surrenders the map. She stalls, then watches him burn a fisher family's boats as an object lesson. Emotional beat: cold clarity; there is no deal worth making with a man like this.

chapters.title: Monsoon Rising
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The monsoon makes landfall days early. They reach Elias at a leper-ward mission on the headwaters just as the first walls of rain arrive; father and daughter reconcile in fragments, and Elias dies at dawn having heard Ada swear to finish what he started. Emotional beat: grief braided with resolve.

chapters.title: Running the Flood
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. With the river rising and Hale's gunboat behind them, Kestrel pilots the Magpie down flooded back-channels no chart records, trusting her memory of every sandbar's mood. A near-capsize costs them their cargo but not the map or the crew. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into mastery — this is what she was born for.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Climax. At the delta tribunal, the boatfolk convene their own court aboard beached hulls. Ada presents the map and Elias's sworn testimony while Hale's men try to seize the Magpie mid-hearing; the river people stand them off. The tribunal voids the magistrate's grants and brands Hale an outlaw. Emotional beat: justice rendered outside the law, paid for in scars.

chapters.title: What the Magpie Carries
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Resolution. Weeks later, the Magpie runs light cargo on a mended river. Ada stays on as partner, mapping the waterways honestly this time; Kestrel burns the ledger of her old debt and keeps only the compass. Emotional beat: quiet arrival — home was never a place, but the people willing to run the flood beside you.
